importantNotes: 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness' (12:9).
'If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come' (5:17) — the declaration of transformation.
Paul's 'thorn in the flesh' (12:7) has been debated for centuries — we don't know what it was.
Chapters 8-9 are the most comprehensive teaching on Christian giving in the NT.
Paul lists his sufferings in detail (11:24-28) — beatings, shipwrecks, dangers everywhere.

chapters.1: God comforts us in affliction so we can comfort others; Paul's changed travel plans.
chapters.2: Forgiveness for the repentant offender; the fragrance of Christ through Paul's ministry.
chapters.3: The glory of the new covenant surpasses the old — written on hearts, not stone.
chapters.4: Treasure in jars of clay — the gospel shines through human weakness; eternal perspective.
chapters.5: The heavenly dwelling; the ministry of reconciliation; 'in Christ, a new creation.'
chapters.6: Do not receive God's grace in vain; Paul's hardships; do not be yoked with unbelievers.
chapters.7: Paul's joy at the Corinthians' repentance; godly sorrow leads to salvation.
chapters.8: The example of the Macedonians' generous giving; Titus sent ahead with the collection.
chapters.9: God loves a cheerful giver; sowing generously reaps generously.
chapters.10: Paul defends his authority; his weapons are not worldly but divinely powerful.
chapters.11: Paul's 'fool's speech' — boasting in his suffering, dangers, and hardships.
chapters.12: Paul's vision of the third heaven; his thorn in the flesh; 'my power is made perfect in weakness.'
chapters.13: Final warnings and encouragement; the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ.
